doc.title: Tangelo: make the weekly shop a two-minute job
doc.author: Noor Haddad, Product
doc.summary: Three parts of the repeat order, each with the problem, the change and the evidence. Six points in all, shipped in three steps.

sourceNote: Screens marked Today and Proposed are schematic drawings of Tangelo. Reference screens are drawings of the fictional apps in the teardown.

sections.title: Home
sections.summary: Put last week's shop, and the staples that are due, on the first screen.
sections.lead: A returning customer opens the app to do one job: repeat last week, with a few changes. Home does not offer that job today.

points.title: Last week's basket is three taps away
points.problem: Repeating a shop means opening Orders, opening the order, then tapping Reorder. Seven of eight customers we spoke to buy mostly the same things each week, and none of them had found that route.
points.change: Put a card at the top of Home: "Your usual shop, 23 items, about $61". One tap opens last week's basket, ready to edit.
points.why: The card opens a basket, never a checkout. A repeat order still needs a look before it is paid for.

constraint.label: Risk from the pre-mortem
constraint.text: A one-tap repeat can shrink baskets, because people stop browsing (R3). Items per order is a guardrail on the test, with a stop line at a 3% fall.

evidence.label: Tangelo today
evidence.caption: Home. Reorder is under Orders, three taps away.

evidence.label: Pippin
evidence.caption: Last week's shop comes first, with its total.

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: The reorder card, above everything else.

know.baseline: Median time from opening the app to placing a repeat order. Not measured yet.
know.expect: More returning customers order within 7 days, and they get there faster.
know.stop: Items per order fall by more than 3%.

points.title: Staples run out between shops
points.problem: Four of eight customers described a second, smaller order midweek for something they forgot. Nothing on Home knows what a customer is about to run out of.
points.change: Add a "Running low?" row with up to three items, chosen from how often this customer buys each one: "Whole milk, every 6 days".

constraint.label: Risk from the pre-mortem
constraint.text: A wrong guess reads as nagging (R7). The row needs at least four past orders of an item before it will show it, and it never shows more than three.

evidence.label: Tangelo today
evidence.caption: Home shows what is popular, not what this customer needs.

evidence.label: Marrow
evidence.caption: A list of the items that are due, from past orders.

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: Three staples at most, shown only when they are due.

know.baseline: Share of orders followed by a smaller order within 3 days.
know.expect: Fewer top-up orders, and slightly larger weekly baskets.
know.stop: More than 1 in 20 customers dismiss the row twice.

sections.title: Basket
sections.summary: Deal with missing items in the basket, where the customer can still choose.
sections.lead: A repeated basket is a week old. Some of it will be out of stock, and today the customer learns that at the worst moment.

points.title: Out-of-stock items surface at the last step
points.problem: Stock is checked when the customer taps Place order. A repeated basket with two missing items fails there, and the customer is sent back to find and remove them.
points.change: Check stock when the basket opens. List what is missing at the top, with one suggested swap each and a Remove button.

constraint.label: Dependency
constraint.text: The stock service has to answer inside one second, or the basket opens without the check and says so (R8). Engineering to confirm the current response time.

evidence.label: Tangelo today
evidence.caption: Checkout. The customer finds out at the last step.

blocks.sub: Go back to your basket to remove them

evidence.label: Pippin
evidence.caption: Stock is checked the moment the basket opens.

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: One suggested swap per missing item, in the basket.

blocks: 2 items are out of stock today

know.baseline: Share of checkouts that hit an out-of-stock error.
know.expect: Out-of-stock errors at checkout fall close to zero.
know.stop: The basket takes more than 1 second longer to open.

points.title: Substitutions are a surprise at the door
points.problem: When an item runs out after the order is placed, the picker chooses a replacement. Five of eight customers had received a swap they did not want, and learned of it when the bags arrived.
points.change: Give every basket line a rule, set once and remembered: swap for something similar, swap for a named item, or do not swap.
points.why: One customer wanted the opposite: "I'd rather get something than nothing." The default stays at similar item, so nobody loses what they have today.

constraint.label: Dependency
constraint.text: Rules add a step for pickers. Operations to estimate the effect on picking time before this is scheduled (R5).

blocks.sub: Tell us within 1 hour for a refund

evidence.label: Marrow
evidence.caption: Asked once per item, then remembered.

blocks: If this is out of stock

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: A rule on every line. Tap to change it.

know.expect: Fewer complaints, and fewer refunds for swaps nobody asked for.
know.stop: Picking time per order rises by more than 5%.

sections.title: Checkout
sections.summary: Settle the slot and the price before the customer has done the work.
sections.lead: Two things can still go wrong after the basket is right: the slot has gone, or the total is not what the customer expected.

points.title: The delivery slot is chosen last, after the work is done
points.problem: Slots are offered at checkout. Four of eight customers had finished a basket and found the slot they wanted was full.
points.change: Show the next three slots on Home. Picking one holds it for 20 minutes, and the basket and checkout both show the held slot.

constraint.label: Risk from the pre-mortem
constraint.text: Held slots that are never used cost capacity (R4). A hold lasts 20 minutes, one per customer, and slot utilisation is a tripwire at 85%.

evidence.label: Tangelo today
evidence.caption: Checkout. The best slot has already gone.

evidence.label: Marrow
evidence.caption: The slot is asked for first, and held.

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: Three slots on Home. Picking one holds it.

blocks: Held for 20 minutes once you start

know.baseline: Share of checkouts where the first slot shown was full.
know.expect: Fewer checkouts abandoned at the slot step.

points.title: The total creeps up with no explanation
points.problem: A repeated basket can cost more than it did last week, and the only sign is a larger total. Three of eight customers said they notice and do not know why.
points.change: Mark each line that costs more than last time with its old price, and add one line to the basket: "3 items cost more than last week. That adds $1.40."

constraint.label: Needs legal review
constraint.text: A was-price is a pricing claim in most markets. Legal to confirm the wording and how long a previous price may be shown (R9). Nothing ships until they have.

evidence.label: Tangelo today
evidence.caption: Checkout shows a total and nothing else.

evidence.label: Sorrel
evidence.caption: Every price that moved is marked.

evidence.label: Proposed
evidence.caption: The difference, in the basket, before checkout.

blocks: 3 items cost more than last week

know.baseline: Contacts about a total that was higher than expected.
know.expect: Fewer price contacts, with no change in checkout completion.
know.stop: Checkout completion falls by more than 1 point.

priorityLead: What each point is meant to move, what it costs, and what could hold it up.

priority.first: Ship behind a switch to half of returning customers for 14 days

priority.change: Stock check when the basket opens
priority.first: Measure the stock service's response time on a full basket
Agree the hold length and the cap with operations
Time ten picks with rules on paper
Check how many customers have four orders of the same item

rolloutLead: Three steps. Each one is only worth shipping if the step before it worked.

rollout.why: The reorder card is only as good as the basket it opens. If that basket has missing items, or the slot has gone, the card makes the experience worse.
Both depend on other teams, picking and legal, and neither blocks the first release.
It needs weeks of order history per customer to be right, and it is the easiest of the six to get wrong.

next: Measure the three baselines for the first release (`1.1`, `2.1`, `3.1`) before the test starts.
Operations to sign off the 20 minute hold and the cap of one held slot per customer (`3.1`).
Engineering to confirm the stock service answers inside one second for a 25 item basket (`2.1`).
Legal to review the was-price wording (`3.2`) before any design time is spent on it.
caveats: Tangelo is a fictional company, and Pippin, Marrow and Sorrel are fictional apps. Every screen here is a schematic drawing and no figure is a real measurement. The counts of customers come from eight fictional interviews.
